name: Rabi' al-Awwal
intro:
The month of Rabi' al-Awwal holds both joy and sorrow within it. The days 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 22, 23 and 25 of this month are memorable days of joy and grief for the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), which we will discuss in detail below.
Joyful events such as the birth of the Prophet (SAWW), Laylat al-Mabit and the Hijra of the Prophet (SAW), his arrival in Medina, the beginning of the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), the birth of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), and the beginning of the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) after the martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (AS) are the unforgettable days of this month. The marriage of the Prophet (SAWW) to Lady Khadija (AS) and the arrival of Lady Ma'suma (AS) in Qom are other days that left joyful memories. The deaths of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Yazid ibn Mu'awiya and Umar ibn Sa'd are further pages from the book of joy of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) in this month.
The beginning of the obligation of prayer, the pillar of the religion of Islam, is another day that will never be forgotten.
On the other hand, a terrible event occurred in this month that was the beginning of all the calamities of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS): the assault on the House of Revelation after the burial of the pure body of the Prophet (SAWW). The first day of Mu'awiya's usurped caliphate, the entry of the household of Imam Husayn (AS) into Syria (Sham), and the destruction of the Ka'ba by Yazid are also among the ominous consequences of Saqifa that took place in this month. The martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (AS) and the passing of Lady Sakina (AS) are also among the events of this month.
Among the battles of the Prophet (SAWW), the Battle of Banu al-Nadir and the Battle of Dumat al-Jandal took place in this month. The peace treaty of Imam Hasan (AS) also took place in this month.
The deaths of Musa, the Abbasid caliph, al-Mu'tasim the Abbasid, Dawud ibn Ali, the tyrannical governor of Medina, Malik ibn Anas and Ahmad ibn Hanbal also occurred in this month.

events.title: Burial of the Pure Body of the Prophet (SAWW)
events.text:
At midnight on the first of Rabi' al-Awwal, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) buried the pure body of the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers (SAWW).
The tragedy and calamity of the passing of the Prophet (SAWW) on the one hand, and the disrespect shown to him and the people's lack of attention to his washing, shrouding and burial on the other, were wounds that weighed heavily on the blessed heart of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). Recalling those bitter days, he said: “Would I have abandoned the noble body of the Prophet (SAW), leaving him unburied, to quarrel over the caliphate and kingship after him?”
Shaykh al-Mufid says: Most of the people did not attend the burial of the Prophet (SAWW) and did not pray over him, because there was a dispute between the Ansar and the Muhajirun over the matter of the caliphate. A'mash says: Their Prophet passed away, and the people had no concern or worry except that some said, “The leader is from us,” and another group said, “The leader is from us.”
At the time of the passing of the Prophet (SAWW), al-Mughira said to Abu Bakr and Umar: If you have any business with the people later, go and catch up with them now. Therefore Abu Bakr and Umar were not present at the burial of the Prophet (SAWW); rather they were among others who were choosing a leader for themselves at Saqifa, and before they came to the side of his body, the pure body had been buried.
Abdullah ibn Hasan says: By God, Abu Bakr and Umar did not pray over the Prophet (SAWW), and his blessed body remained unburied for three days, yet despite all this the people of Saqifa were busy with their own affairs.
Imam al-Baqir (AS) says: The people prayed over his body on Monday and the night of Tuesday, and the general public, even the notables and those close to him, prayed over his blessed body, but none of the people of Saqifa attended his washing, shrouding and burial. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) sent Buraida al-Aslami to inform them, but they paid no heed, and after his burial their allegiance was also completed.
Aisha has a noteworthy admission in this regard. She said: “By God, we did not learn of the burial of the Prophet (SAWW) until we heard the sound of shovels and pickaxes from his chamber on the night of Wednesday,” meaning that we realized only after the burial.
One must ask these people, who forgot everything over the usurpation of the caliphate:
Was Saqifa held in the presence of the Prophet (SAWW) and at his instruction, or was Ghadir?
Did an order come from God to form the council of Saqifa, or was it concerning Ghadir?
Were most of the Muslim lands represented at Saqifa, or at Ghadir?
Were all the people present at Saqifa, or at Ghadir, where even the women pledged allegiance?
sources: Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: vol. 2, p. 78. Musnad Ahmad: vol. 6, pp. 62, 242, 274. Sunan al-Bayhaqi: vol. 3, p. 409. Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (Ibn Kathir): vol. 4, p. 538.
Al-Khisal: p. 372. Al-Ikhtisas: p. 171.
Al-Ihtijaj: p. 74.
Irshad al-Mufid: vol. 1, p. 189.
Taqrib al-Ma'arif: p. 256.
Al-Musannaf: p. 14, 568. Jami' al-Ahadith: vol. 13, p. 267.
Taqrib al-Ma'arif: p. 251.

events.title: Laylat al-Mabit (The Night of the Sleeping)
events.text:
On the first night of this month, the Prophet (SAWW) migrated from Mecca to Medina to escape the evil of the unbelievers. That night, our master and lord Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) sacrificed himself and slept in the bed of the noble Messenger of Islam (SAWW) in his place, since the Quraysh unbelievers intended to kill him. On this occasion the verse “ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله ...” (“And among the people is he who sells his life seeking the pleasure of God, and God is kind to His servants”) was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS).
On the night when Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) slept in place of the Prophet (SAWW), Gabriel and Michael were addressed: I have made brotherhood between the two of you. Which of you will sacrifice so that the other may have a long life? Both chose the long life.
The call came: “Look at the earth and see how Ali (AS) sacrificed his life for his brother the Prophet (SAW), slept in his place and offered his life for his life. Go down to the earth and protect him from the enemies.” They came, and Gabriel sat at the head of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and Michael at his feet, and called out: Bakh bakh, man mithluka ya ibn Abi Talib (Bravo, bravo! Who is like you, O son of Abu Talib!) — God has boasted of you before the assembly of angels. It was here that the noble verse “ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله ...” was revealed.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 8. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 27. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 201. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 332. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 168. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596.
Surah al-Baqarah: verse 207.

events.title: Hijra of the Prophet (SAWW)
events.text: The Prophet (SAWW) migrated to Medina the Pure thirteen years after the Bi'tha (the beginning of his mission).
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 8. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596.

events.title: The Assault on the House of Revelation
events.text:
On this day the first assault on the house of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) took place. When Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) attended to the washing, shrouding and burial of the Prophet while the usurpers of the caliphate were at Saqifa, on Wednesday night, which was the first of Rabi', he buried his blessed body and, in accordance with the testament of the Prophet (SAWW), turned to the compilation of the Qur'an. The Prophet had told him: “Dear Ali, do not leave the house for three days and compile the Qur'an...”
During these days the house was attacked three times: The first time was on the first day of Rabi', when they came to demand allegiance, and he said that he had sworn not to leave the house until the compilation of the Qur'an was complete, and they returned. After that, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) would take al-Siddiqa al-Tahira (AS) and Hasan and Husayn (AS) at night to the doors of the Companions' houses and ask for their help.
The second time was seven days after the burial of the Prophet (SAW), when Zubayr and a number of others had gathered at the house of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). That day Zubayr drew his sword to kill Umar.
The third time they attacked the house and, after setting fire to the door of the house, beating and injuring al-Siddiqa al-Tahira (AS) and killing Hazrat Muhsin (AS), they took Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) out with his hands bound.
sources: Tafsir Furat: p. 398. In Tawhid al-Saduq: p. 73 it is seven days, and in Amali al-Tusi: vol. 1, p. 263 it is nine days.
Kitab Sulaym: p. 128. Al-Ihtijaj: pp. 75 - 190.
Tawhid al-Saduq: p. 73. Al-Ihtijaj: vol. 1, pp. 95 - 111. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 28, p. 321.

events.title: Poisoning of Imam al-Askari (AS)
events.text:
Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS) was poisoned and his illness began.
According to one account, the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS) in the year 260 AH took place on this day.
According to another account it was on the fourth of Rabi' al-Awwal, and according to yet another, on the eighth of Rabi' al-Awwal.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 2. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: p. 523. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 732. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 201. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 336. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2, p. 415. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, pp. 334 - 335.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 2. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: p. 523. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 732. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 201.
Masar al-Shi'a: pp. 28 - 29. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 205.

events.title: Destruction of the Ka'ba by Yazid
events.text: In the year 64 AH, by Yazid's order, the House of the Ka'ba was destroyed with a catapult. This calamity took place eleven days before the death of Yazid.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 63. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 203.

events.title: Passing of Lady Sakina (AS)
events.text:
Lady Sakina (AS), the daughter of Imam Husayn (AS), passed away in Medina on the night of the fifth of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 117 AH, 56 years after the event of Karbala.
Her mother was Lady Rabab (AS); the two of them were together at Karbala and accompanied the captives all the way to Kufa and Sham.
On the morning of her passing, Muhammad ibn Abdullah (al-Nafs al-Zakiyya) bought four hundred dinars' worth of perfume and aloeswood and burned it in censers around her coffin. Khalid ibn Abd al-Malik, the governor of Medina, who intended that, with the funeral delayed because of the heat of the weather, disrespect would be shown to her pure body, said: “Wait, I will come to pray over the body.” But he did not come. Hence her blessed body was not buried until night. After that, Imam al-Sajjad (AS) — and according to another account Yahya ibn Hasan (AS), and according to another Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Nafs al-Zakiyya — prayed over her body and buried her with honor.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 26. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 206. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 67. Mustadrakat 'Ilm Rijal al-Hadith: vol. 8, p. 580. Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, p. 280.
Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 205 - 206. Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, pp. 280 - 282.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (AS)
events.text:
Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS) was martyred in the year 260 AH at the age of 28 at the hands of al-Mu'tamid the Abbasid. Al-Mu'tamid used to instruct the Abbasids to treat him harshly. Saduq (RA) says: Al-Mu'tamid imprisoned Imam al-Askari (AS) several times.
He was 22 years old when Imam al-Hadi (AS) was martyred, and the period of his Imamate was six years. On the night before the day he was martyred, he had written many letters to the people of Medina.
At the time of the dawn prayer, after Imam al-Asr (the Imam of the Age) (AS) performed ablution for him and gave him a decoction to drink, he was martyred.
When the people of Samarra learned of it, all the bazaars were closed and the people gathered around his house. The ministers and followers of the caliph, the Banu Hashim and the Alawite women were inside the house. In Samarra the sound of wailing and weeping was heard from every side, and it was as if the Day of Resurrection had begun.
Imam al-Zaman (AS) washed him, and after he was shrouded, the pure body was brought for the prayer. His brother Ja'far came forward to pray over the blessed body. As soon as he was about to say the takbir, Imam al-Zaman (AS), a wheat-complexioned child with curly hair and spaced teeth like a piece of the moon, came out of the room, pulled Ja'far's cloak and moved him away from that place, and prayed over his noble father; and they buried him next to the grave of his noble father Imam al-Hadi (AS).
Ja'far reported this event to al-Mu'tamid. They searched everywhere for the Imam, but found no trace of him.
In the year of the martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (AS) — the year 260 AH — the eminent hadith scholar Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Nishaburi passed away: he was the author of 180 works, and Imam al-Askari (AS) invoked God's mercy upon him three times.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 336. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2, p. 402. Mustajad: p. 226. Iqbal: p. 598. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 207. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 334. Al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 561. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, pp. 355 - 356; vol. 50, p. 334.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 144.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 5, p. 331.
Ghaybat al-Tusi: p. 164. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 334. Kamal al-Din: p. 473.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 209.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, pp. 143 - 144. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 350 - 351.

events.title: Beginning of the Imamate of Hazrat Wali al-Asr (AS)
events.text:
The beginning of the Imamate of Hazrat Sahib al-Amr (AS) and his Minor Occultation (al-Ghayba al-Sughra) came after the martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (AS), whose only child he was.
This day is a Shi'a Eid and the first day of the Imamate and caliphate of the last caliph, the true Proof (Hujja) and savior of mankind, Hazrat Baqiyyat Allah al-A'zam (AS), in the year 260 AH.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 336. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2, p. 402. Mustajad: p. 226. Iqbal: p. 598. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 207. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 334. Al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 561. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, pp. 355 - 356; vol. 50, p. 334.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 211.

events.title: Killing of Umar ibn al-Khattab
events.text:
At the end of the night of the ninth of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 23 AH, Umar ibn al-Khattab died; the Sunni view is that it was Wednesday, the 26th of Dhu al-Hijja.
This day is a day of joy for the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), the prophets, the angels, the inhabitants of the highest heavens ('Illiyyin), the friends of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and his pure descendants, because on this day the curse of Hazrat al-Siddiqa al-Kubra Fatima al-Zahra (AS) was answered. It is a day of great stature, a day of joy for the Shi'a and their great Eid. The Messenger of God (SAWW) made this day an Eid and commanded that the people also make it an Eid and perform its acts.
Whoever gives charity on this day, God will forgive him. On this day it is recommended (mustahabb) to feed one's fellow believers, to perfume them, to be generous to one's family, to wear new clothes, to give thanks to God Almighty, and to perform worship.
Virtues and names have been mentioned for this day, among them: the Greatest Eid of God, the Second Ghadir, the Second Eid al-Fitr, the Day of the Joy of the Shi'a, the Eid of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), the Day of the Killing of the Hypocrite, the Day of the Acceptance of Deeds, the Day of the Victory of the Oppressed, the Day of the Friendship of the Believers, the Day of Avoiding Major Sins, the Day of the Destruction of Misguidance and Error, the Day of Thanksgiving.
sources: Madinat al-Ma'ajiz: vol. 2, p. 97.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 334. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal and Rabi' al-Thani, p. 59. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 67.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 211.
Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 189. Zad al-Ma'ad: pp. 334 - 344. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, pp. 351 - 356 (from Zawa'id al-Fawa'id of Sayyid Ibn Tawus).

subsections.title: The Story of the Killing of Umar
subsections.text:
Umar ibn al-Khattab was stabbed several times with a dagger by Abu Lu'lu'a, whose name was Firuz and who was a slave of Mughira ibn Shu'ba, which led to his death.
According to the well-known account, when Abu Lu'lu'a struck Umar and tried to flee, some people blocked him, and he wounded 12 people, six of whom died.
The story was as follows: before the takbir of the prayer, Abu Lu'lu'a came forward and struck Umar one blow on the shoulder and another on the flank. Umar fell, and some people gathered and carried him to his house. It was nearly sunrise when Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf led the people in prayer.
Umar on his deathbed
When they took Umar to his house, some nabidh was brought and he drank it, but it came out from the wounded places, and it could not be determined where it was coming out from, since it was the same color as blood. So some said: Let the caliph drink milk, because it is white and it will be clear. He drank the milk and it came out from the places of the wounds. Those present, to console him, said: “It is no problem, it will do no harm!” But the blows of Abu Lu'lu'a took effect, and he joined the former caliph. On the third day he was buried beside Abu Bakr.
Umar ruled as caliph for ten years, six months and four nights. He was the first to call himself Amir al-Mu'minin, and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari was the first to address him by this title from the pulpit.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 23. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 33. Al-'Idda al-Qawiyya: p. 328. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 129. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 199.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 34.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 200
Tarikh al-Khulafa': pp. 133 - 134.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 11.

subsections.title: Umar's Innovation (Bid'a) Concerning the Future of the Caliphate
subsections.text:
Umar said to Ibn Abbas: To whom shall I entrust this caliphate? He suggested Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) and said: His courage, virtue, kinship and precedence in Islam are well known. Umar said: He has a streak of joking in his nature! Ibn Abbas said: What do you say about Uthman? Umar said: If he becomes caliph, he will set the Banu Umayya over the necks of the people.
Ibn Abbas said: What do you say about Talha? Umar said: He is an arrogant man; he hurt the Prophet with a remark he made on the day the verse of hijab was revealed. When the verse of hijab was revealed he had said: “When he passes away, we will marry his wives.”
Ibn Abbas said: What do you say about Zubayr ibn al-Awwam? He said: He is a brave man, but very miserly. He is a bad-tempered and corrupt man, sometimes a human being and sometimes an unbeliever. Regarding Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas he said: He is an arrogant and fanatical man and is not fit for the work of the caliphate. Ibn Abbas said: And what is your opinion of Abd al-Rahman? Umar said: He is a weak-hearted man.
At the time of his death Umar left the matter of the caliphate to a shura (council) and summoned Abu Talha al-Ansari and said to him: After my death, take fifty of the Ansar with drawn swords and bring six men together in the house of Aisha: Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), Uthman, Talha, Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Then give them three days, and after that, if four or five of them agree on one view and one or two oppose them, kill the opponents; and if three have one view and three another, give precedence to the side in which Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf is and strike off the necks of the other three; and if after three days they do not agree on a matter, strike off the necks of all six.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 152 - 153. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 143.

subsections.title: The Shura After the Death of Umar
subsections.text:
After the death of Umar a shura was formed in the house of Aisha, and Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, the son of Safiyya, gave up his right to his cousin Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)! Talha ibn Ubaydullah also gave up his right to Uthman!! Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas also gave up his right to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.
Abd al-Rahman came to the mosque and, in the gathering of the Companions, said to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS): I will pledge allegiance to you on the condition that you act according to the Book of God, the Sunna of the Prophet (SAWW) and the way of Abu Bakr and Umar! Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said: Rather, I will act according to the Book of God, the Sunna of the Prophet (SAWW) and the exercise of my own judgment.
Abd al-Rahman said these words to Uthman three times, and Uthman accepted. The third time Abd al-Rahman pledged allegiance to Uthman and the others pledged allegiance as well, except for the Banu Hashim and a group of the eminent Companions such as Ammar ibn Yasir and Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who did not pledge allegiance.
Here it is appropriate to raise several questions:
What occupation was Umar engaged in during his youth, and what job did he have on his trading journeys?
At the Battle of Hudaybiyya and elsewhere, who objected to the Prophet (SAWW)?
Who accused the Prophet (SAWW) of delirium?
Who set fire to the door of the house of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and said: “I intend to burn the house down with its people, even if Fatima is in it”?
Who killed Muhsin ibn Ali (AS)?
Who ordered Qunfudh to whip the daughter of the Prophet (SAWW)?
Who encouraged Abu Bakr to usurp Fadak and rejected the testimony of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), Umm Ayman, and Hasan and Husayn (AS)?
Who took the deed of Fadak from Lady al-Siddiqa (AS) and showed disrespect to her blessed face?
Who was the first to introduce folding the hands in prayer?
Who was the first to refer the caliphate to a shura?
Who was the first, together with Abu Bakr, to withhold the share of the relatives (dhawi al-qurba)?
Who was the first, on the day of Eid al-Ghadir, to pledge allegiance to Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), saying: Bakh bakh, ya ibn Abi Talib, asbahta mawlaya wa mawla kulli mu'minin wa mu'mina (Bravo, O son of Abu Talib, you have become my master and the master of every believing man and woman)?
Who was the first to perform ablution from the jug of the Christians and consider them pure?
Who was the first to invalidate the testimony of a slave?
Who was the first to forbid the mut'a of Hajj and the mut'a of women?
Who was the first to order that the voluntary (nafila) prayers of the month of Ramadan be performed in congregation?
Who was the first to say that non-Arabs do not inherit from one another?
Why did a person become intoxicated when he drank from the caliph's jug?!
Who was it whose estate, when one-eighth of it was divided among his four wives after his death, gave each wife 83,000 dinars?
Who said: “Everyone is more learned than I, even old women”?!
Who was it that, whenever he was asked a question and was left without an answer, would say: Being busy with brokerage and trade prevented me from learning the rulings?
The fact that the history books state, in various phrasings, that Umar ibn al-Khattab was appointed to the caliphate of the Muslims according to Abu Bakr's testament raises several questions:
1- Is Abu Bakr's testament binding, while the testament of the noblest of creation, the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), at Ghadir and elsewhere, is not binding?
2- At the time of his passing, did the Prophet (SAWW) not say: Bring paper and pen so that I may say something that will be written down, so that you will not disagree after me? Why did they accuse him of delirium and not bring paper and pen, when God says in the Qur'an: “Whatever he says is revelation, not from himself”? How was it that paper and pen were brought for Abu Bakr and no one objected? Interestingly, he kept losing consciousness and regaining it, and after the “Bismillah” Uthman wrote on his own that the caliph after Abu Bakr is Umar, and Abu Bakr did not object?
sources: Surah al-Najm: verses 3 - 4. وما ينطق عن الهوى إن هو إلا وحي يوحى (“Nor does he speak from his own desire. It is nothing but a revelation revealed.”)

events.title: Killing of Umar ibn Sa'd
events.text: Umar ibn Sa'd, the tyrannical commander of Yazid's army, was dispatched to Hell on this day at the hands of Mukhtar al-Thaqafi (RA)
sources: Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 344.

events.title: Marriage of the Prophet (SAWW) to Lady Khadija (AS)
events.text:
The Prophet (SAWW) married Lady Khadija al-Kubra (AS) 15 years before the Hijra. From Shi'a hadiths and Sunni reports it is clear that Khadija bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad was renowned for her knowledge and awareness of the books of that time. Among the women of Quraysh, besides the abundance of wealth, properties and trade that she had, she was distinguished by intellect and shrewdness, and at that time she was called Tahira (the Pure), Mubaraka (the Blessed), Sayyidat al-Nisa' (Mistress of Women) and Queen of the Bat'ha (Mecca). She was among those who awaited the coming of the Prophet (SAWW) and always asked the scholars about the signs of his prophethood.
When she was honored to meet the Prophet (SAWW), she first asked about the seal of prophethood and beheld it, and her eloquent poems in praise of the noble Messenger of Islam (SAWW) and her perfect love for the family of Abd al-Muttalib are famous, which reveal her knowledge, refinement and love. On the very day he was appointed to the mission, Lady Khadija (AS) believed.
Lady Khadija (AS) traded with her own wealth and the inheritance she had received, on a mudaraba (profit-sharing) basis. It was not long before she became one of the great merchants, such that eighty thousand camels were under the load of her trade, and her wealth increased every day. On the roof of her house there was a dome of green silk with silk ropes and several figures, which was a sign of the dignity of that noble lady.
Many people, such as Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt and Ibn Abi Shihab, each of whom had four hundred maidservants, slaves and attendants, and Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan and other great men of the Arabs of that day, came to ask for her hand; but she did not accept. Finally Lady Khadija (AS) herself proposed marriage to the Prophet (SAWW), and this marriage was carried out with special customs and ceremonies.
God granted her two sons, named Qasim and Abdullah, who were also called Tayyib and Tahir, and four daughters, named Umm Kulthum, Zaynab, Ruqayya and Fatima (AS); and she is the grandmother of the Infallibles (AS).
Lady Khadija (AS) lived with the Prophet (SAWW) for twenty-four years and one month, and as long as she was alive the Prophet (SAWW) took no other wife. Lady Khadija (AS) also handed over all her wealth to the Prophet (SAWW). Aisha says: It rarely happened that the Prophet (SAWW) left the house without mentioning Khadija with praise, so much so that one day the fire of my jealousy was kindled and I said: O Messenger of God, how long will you keep mentioning Khadija? She was nothing but an old woman! God has given you better than her (meaning herself)! The Prophet (SAWW) became angry at my words and said: No, by God! I have not been given better than Khadija (AS). She believed in me when the people were unbelievers, and she confirmed my prophethood when the people were denying me, and she placed her wealth at my disposal when the people were keeping me away from themselves. God Almighty granted me children through Khadija and made your womb barren.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 211. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 67. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 20. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 344. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 732. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 357.
Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 2, pp. 202, 207, 211.

events.title: Death of Dawud ibn Ali, the Tyrannical Governor of Medina
events.text: Dawud ibn Ali, the paternal uncle of al-Saffah, perished in Medina on the tenth of Rabi' al-Awwal through the supplication of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), because Dawud ibn Ali had ordered that Mu'alla ibn Khunays, one of the companions of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), be martyred.
sources: Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 732. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 344. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 67.

events.title: Death of Malik ibn Anas
events.text: On this day in the year 179 AH, Malik ibn Anas al-Asbahi, the head of the Maliki school, one of the four Sunni schools of jurisprudence, died and was buried in al-Baqi'. Among his peculiarities is that he remained in his mother's womb for three years after his father's death and was born after three years!!?
sources: Rawdat al-Jannat: vol. 7, p. 224.

events.title: First Day of Mu'awiya's Usurped Caliphate
events.text: On this day in the year 41 AH, Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan installed himself as caliph and took allegiance from the people; he was the first Umayyad caliph after Uthman.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 7.

events.title: Beginning of the Obligation of Prayer
events.text: In the first year of the Hijra, on this day, prayer became obligatory both at home and while traveling.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 30. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 55.

events.title: Arrival of the Prophet (SAWW) in Medina
events.text: At sunset of this day, after migrating from Mecca, the Prophet (SAWW) entered Medina the Pure; he alighted at Quba and waited until Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) joined him, and then they entered Medina. This was after, on the 4th of Rabi' al-Awwal, the Prophet (SAWW) had come out of the Cave of Thawr on the route of the Hijra and set off toward Medina.
sources: Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 732. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 344; Masar al-Shi'a: p. 29. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 7. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 168; vol. 19, pp. 104 - 125.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 28. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 21.

events.title: Death of al-Mu'tasim the Abbasid
events.text:
On Thursday the twelfth of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 227 AH, two hours after nightfall, al-Mu'tasim the Abbasid perished in Samarra. The cause of his death was that he had himself cupped (hijama) and then developed a fever, and with that fever he hastened to Hell.
Among his greatest crimes is the martyrdom of Imam al-Jawad (AS).
The length of his caliphate was 8 years, 8 months and 8 days, and he was the eighth of the Abbasid caliphs. He had 8 sons and 8 daughters and built 8 palaces. Al-Mu'tasim was a tyrannical man and had no share in learning, refinement or writing. He inflicted many injuries on the Sayyids, especially their elders, and during his rule he had great interest in constructing buildings.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 297 - 310. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 216.

events.title: Death of Ahmad ibn Hanbal
events.text: On this day in the year 241 AH, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the head of the Hanbalis, died in Baghdad and was buried in the same city. His ancestor was Dhu al-Thudayya, the leader of the Kharijites of Nahrawan, who was sent to Hell at the hands of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). According to one account his death was in Rabi' al-Thani.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 72. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, p. 120. Rawdat al-Jannat: vol. 1, p. 185.
Rawdat al-Jannat: vol. 1, p. 184.
Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, p. 123.
Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, p. 120.

events.title: Death of Yazid ibn Mu'awiya
events.text:
In the year 64 AH, on the night of the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, Yazid ibn Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, at the age of 39 or 37, hastened to the depths of Hell. Other views on the death of Yazid are the twelfth and the fifteenth of this month.
Yazid's mother was Maysun, the daughter of Bahdal al-Kalbi. She is the one who yielded herself to her father's slave, and she conceived the accursed Yazid. For this reason, according to the words of the Imams (AS), the killer of Imam Husayn (AS) is illegitimate (walad al-zina), and this statement also includes Shimr, Umar ibn Sa'd, Ibn Ziyad and others.
He was a wine-drinker, a gambler, a keeper of monkeys, one who had relations with close female relatives (mahram), a composer of blasphemous poetry, and an abandoner of prayer. It was he who brought about the heart-rending event of Karbala and martyred Imam Husayn (AS) and the Ahl al-Bayt and companions, and took Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the aunt of the Sayyids Zaynab al-Kubra (AS) and other Alawite and Fatimid women into captivity in that condition through the lanes and bazaars.
It was he who destroyed the House of God and burned the covering of the Ka'ba. It was also he who, in the event of Harra in Medina, exposed the women of the Muhajirun and Ansar, and for three days made the property, lives and honor of the people lawful for his soldiers. After this event children were born who had no known father. After that there was killing and plunder in Medina and the sanctity of the noble Prophetic sanctuary was violated, and people were killed inside the pure sanctuary.
There are several accounts of the cause of his death: one is that he perished of a sudden affliction. Shaykh Saduq (RA) says: Yazid went to sleep one night in a drunken state and in the morning he was found dead, his body altered as if tar had been smeared on it. His ill-omened body was buried at Bab al-Saghir in Damascus.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal and a group of Sunnis have permitted cursing Yazid, and some of them believe in the unbelief of Yazid, and Ibn al-Jawzi wrote a book refuting Yazid.
On this day, visiting Imam Husayn (AS) is recommended.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4. Taqwim al-Muhsinin: p. 16. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 215. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 345. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 189; vol. 98, p. 101. 'Awalim (Maqtal): p. 224. Tawdih al-Maqasid: pp. 7 - 8. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 55.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 29.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 55 - 56.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 216.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 98, p. 201.

events.title: Death of Musa, the Abbasid Caliph
events.text:
On this day — and according to another account on the 15th or 18th of Rabi' al-Awwal — Musa al-Hadi, son of al-Mahdi the Abbasid, hastened to the depths of Hell. On that same night Harun became caliph and al-Ma'mun was also born. The caliphate of Musa al-Hadi lasted one year and three months, and he lived 25 or 26 years. He was famous for cruelty, hardness of heart, lack of mercy, harshness of temperament and wickedness of soul.
Sayyid Ibn Tawus (RA) relates in Muhaj al-Da'awat that Musa al-Hadi sent an army which martyred Husayn ibn Ali ibn Hasan al-Muthanna ibn Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS), the Master of Fakhkh, with his companions, and his head was brought along with the captives before him; when his gaze fell on that head, he recited some verses.
Then the captives were brought one after another, and after reproaching and rebuking them he ordered them killed. In one day he killed a group of the descendants of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and he kept cursing the Talibids until he reached the blessed name of Musa ibn Ja'far (AS); he spoke ill of him and cried out that Husayn, the Master of Fakhkh, did not rise except by the command of Musa ibn Ja'far (AS), because he is the holder of the testament in this family. By God, I will kill him. May God kill me if I leave him alive, and may God kill me if I pardon him; and had it not been that al-Saffah and the father of al-Mahdi related to me many virtues about Ja'far ibn Muhammad because of the abundance of his knowledge, religion and virtue, I would surely have opened his grave and burned his body in fire.
Ali ibn Yaqtin sent a letter from Baghdad to Hazrat al-Kazim (AS) and described the situation. When the letter reached the Imam, he informed his household and Shi'a and said: What is your opinion in this matter?
They said: The best course is for you to hide yourself from this tyrannical oppressor. The Imam said: The first letter that comes from Iraq will contain the news of the death of Musa al-Hadi; and so it happened, as the Imam had reported.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 89. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 215. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 223.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 91.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 222 - 224.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 92.

events.title: Arrival of the Household of Imam Husayn (AS) in Sham
events.text: According to one account, 66 days after the day of Ashura, the household of Imam Husayn (AS) entered Sham.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 219.

events.title: Birth of the Prophet (SAWW)
events.text:
By the agreement of the Shi'a scholars, on this day, at dawn on Friday, in blessed Mecca, the auspicious birth of the Master of the Prophets, Muhammad al-Mustafa (SAWW), took place. His birth coincided with the reign of Anushirvan the Just, and in that year the People of the Elephant were destroyed.
His name is Muhammad (SAWW) and his kunya is Abu al-Qasim. His father's name is Abdullah and his mother's name is Amina bint Wahb.
At the time of his birth, light shone from his forehead and the fragrance of musk emanated from him. That night a light shone from the direction of the Hijaz and spread throughout the whole world. The thrones of kings were overturned, and all of them were mute that day and could not speak.
The angels brought near and the spirits of the chosen prophets attended at his birth, and Ridwan, the keeper of Paradise, descended with the houris, and they brought ewers and basins of gold, silver and emerald of Paradise, and brought sherbets from Paradise for Lady Amina, which she drank. After his birth he was washed with the waters of Paradise and perfumed with the fragrances of Firdaws.
sources: Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 1, p. 14. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 42. Tahdhib: vol. 6, p. 2. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 345. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 9. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 733. Al-'Idda al-Qawiyya: p. 110. Masari' al-Shuhada' wa Maqatil al-Su'ada': p. 23. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 220. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 17, p. 280; vol. 55, p. 361; vol. 95, p. 194.
A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, pp. 33 - 44. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 1, p. 15. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 30.
Haqq al-Yaqin: p. 27.

subsections.title: Miracles of His Birth
subsections.text:
On the day of his birth, every idol anywhere in the world fell on its face, and fourteen battlements of the Iwan of Kisra (Khosrow) collapsed. The lake of Sawa, which was worshipped, dried up and turned into a salt flat. In the valley of Sawa, where for years no one had seen water, water flowed. The Fire Temple of Fars, which had not been extinguished for a thousand years, was extinguished on the night of his birth. The knowledge of the soothsayers and the magic of the sorcerers was nullified, and the arch of Kisra split in two from the middle, as is visible to this day.
At the time of his birth this call was heard from the heavens: “The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish.”
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 100.
Surah al-Isra': verse 84. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 101.

subsections.title: Characteristics of the Prophet (SAWW)
subsections.text:
Flies never settled on his blessed body. Whenever his blessed eyes were asleep, his heart was awake, and he saw and heard as he did when awake. He saw behind him just as he saw in front of him.
Whatever animal he rode never grew old or thin. He had a donkey named Ya'fur. Whenever he commanded it: Bring such-and-such a man, it would go to the man's door, knock its head on the door and by gesture bring him.
Among the peculiarities of the birth of the Prophet (SAWW) was that he was born circumcised, with the umbilical cord cut, and clean of blood and other impurities. Also at the time of birth he came out feet first, not head first. At the time of birth he fell in prostration facing the Ka'ba, and when he raised his head from prostration he lifted his hand toward the sky and affirmed the oneness of God and his own messengership, and then a light shone from him that illuminated the east and west of the world.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 110.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 112.
Haqq al-Yaqin: p. 26.

subsections.title: Miracles of the Prophet (SAWW)
subsections.text:
The Prophet (SAWW) had many miracles, among which are the following examples:
1- The acceptance of his supplication in bringing the dead back to life, giving sight to the blind and healing the sick.
2- His speaking with animals.
3- Knowledge of all languages and the ability to speak in all of them.
4- The seal of prophethood was set on his blessed back and its light exceeded the light of the sun.
5- Water flowed from between his blessed fingers, to such an extent that a large crowd had their thirst quenched.
6- Pebbles in his blessed hand glorified God and the people heard them.
7- His holy body cast no shadow in the sunlight.
8- Whenever he cast his blessed saliva into a well, blessing came to that well and it filled with water. He would rub his blessed saliva on anyone with pain and they would be healed.
9- Whatever food his blessed hand touched became blessed, and from a little food he satisfied a great multitude.
10- Whenever he walked on soft ground his footprint did not remain, and when he walked on hard rock the imprint of his blessed foot remained.
The day of the birth of the Prophet is a noble and blessed day which, from ancient times, the righteous of the family of Muhammad (SAWW) have honored, fulfilling the right of this day and fasting. Whoever fasts on the 17th of Rabi' al-Awwal, God Almighty grants him the reward of a year of fasting. On this day it is recommended to give charity, visit the holy shrines, perform good deeds and bring joy to the believers.
sources: Haqq al-Yaqin: pp. 26 - 27.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 30.

events.title: Birth of Imam al-Sadiq (AS)
events.text:
On the 17th of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 83 AH, the auspicious birth of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) took place in Medina the Illuminated.
His blessed name is Ja'far, his noble kunya is Abu Abdillah and his luminous title is al-Sadiq. His noble father is Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS), and his honored mother is Lady Umm Farwa, about whom Imam al-Sadiq (AS) says: “My mother was among the pious, believing and virtuous women.”
Imam al-Sadiq (AS) had seven sons and three daughters, who are: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), Isma'il, Abdullah, Muhammad al-Dibaj, Ishaq, Ali al-Uraydi, Abbas, Umm Farwa, Asma', Fatima.
In describing his appearance it is said: He was of medium height, with a radiant face, white complexion and a long nose; his hair was black and curly and he had a black mole on his cheek.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 514. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 179. Tarikh al-A'imma: p. 10. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 30. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 9. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 194. Al-'Idda al-Qawiyya: p. 147. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 222.
Al-Kafi: vol. 1, p. 472.
Al-Manaqib: vol. 4, p. 280.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 2, p. 121.

events.title: Battle of Banu al-Nadir
events.text: In the third year of the Hijra the expedition (ghazwa) of Banu al-Nadir took place and the Jews were expelled from Medina.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 9. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 223. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 207.

events.title: Arrival of Lady Ma'suma (AS) in Qom
events.text:
On this day in the year 201 AH, the Karima of the Ahl al-Bayt, Lady Fatima Ma'suma (AS), came to Qom, which was 17 days before her passing.
With her blessed arrival she blessed this city, and at the request of Musa ibn Khazraj, son of Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who was one of the notables of Qom, she illuminated his house and alighted there. She stayed in that same place, and the women of Qom, especially the Alawite women, came into her service and benefited from her presence until after 17 days she passed away. Her place of worship is known as “Sittiyya” and is famous in Mir Square in Qom.
sources: Given that her passing was on the 10th of Rabi' al-Thani and she stayed 17 days in Qom, the 23rd of Rabi' al-Awwal is the anniversary of her arrival in Qom.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 60, p. 219.

events.title: Battle of Dumat al-Jandal
events.text:
On this day in the fifth year of the Hijra, during the time of the Prophet (SAWW), the expedition of Dumat al-Jandal took place. In the lands of “Dumat al-Jandal” a group of villains had joined forces and were attacking caravans. On the 25th of Rabi' al-Awwal the Prophet (SAWW) appointed Siba' ibn Urfuta al-Ghifari as his deputy in Medina, and set out with a thousand warriors until they reached those regions. When the highway robbers realized that he was coming, they fled. The Muslims took their possessions and entered Medina on the twentieth of Rabi' al-Thani.
Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla says: I was passing by Dumat al-Jandal with Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Abu Musa said to me: When we reached Dumat al-Jandal with the Prophet (SAW), he said to me: “In this place two men of the Children of Israel ruled unjustly, and soon two men from my community will rule unjustly in this place.”
The narrator says: Abu Musa and Amr ibn al-As went to Dumat al-Jandal for the arbitration at Siffin and gave judgment between Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) and the accursed Mu'awiya. After the affair of the two arbiters I met Abu Musa and said to him: “Were you not the one who narrated such a hadith from the Prophet (SAWW)?!” He said: By God, it is God whose help is sought!!
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 150.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 150.
Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 150.

events.title: Peace Treaty of Imam Hasan (AS)
events.text:
The agreement of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS) with the accursed Mu'awiya was on the 25th of Rabi' al-Awwal, and some have reported it as the 26th of this month; it included the following:
1- They must not curse Ali (AS).
2- The blood of the Shi'a must be respected and protected, and their rights must not be trampled.
3- Mu'awiya must distribute one million dirhams among the orphans of the Battles of the Camel (Jamal) and Siffin.
4- The Imam (AS) would not call Mu'awiya Amir al-Mu'minin.
5- Mu'awiya must act according to the Book of God and the Sunna of the Prophet (SAWW).
6- After his death, Mu'awiya must not hand the caliphate over to someone else.
Mu'awiya accepted these conditions and other conditions related to the preservation of Islam, especially the Shi'a, and the war ended, but that accursed man did not abide by any of the terms of this agreement; rather, he acted contrary to all of them.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 40 - 41.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 225. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rabi' al-Awwal, p. 155. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 213.
Irshad: vol. 2, p. 14. Maqatil al-Talibiyyin: p. 26. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 65. 3 - 2.

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
